preview: Abhishek Gupta shares his internship interview experience at Morgan Stanley, detailing the online assessment, technical round, HR round, and helpful preparation tips.
content: Morgan Stanley Interview Experience Abhishek Gupta | T.Y.B.Tech 2020-24 Overview : On 25th July TPO forwarded the internship announcements of various companies and Morgan Stanley was among them. (I was shocked as I was expecting internship interviews in September 🙂.) Eligibility Criteria: 1. Circuital Branch Student 2. CGPA ≥ 7.5 Online Assessment: An online Assessment was conducted on 27th July on the AMCAT Platform. There were three sections. 1. Coding Section: There were three questions to be solved in 60 mins. Q1. I don’t remember the exact question but it was a simple question we were supposed to figure out a greedy strategy. I was able to solve it but as I was not able to understand the problem statement in the first go I solved it in the end. Q2. The second question was to print the boundary order traversal of a tree. I was able to solve it and It was overall an easy problem (or it was easy for me). After discussing it with my friends I found out that although they knew it was boundary order traversal, they didn’t know how to take the input. Q3. Actually, I didn’t get the time even to read the problem as I spent like 40mins on 2nd question but after discussing it with my friends I came to know that it was the easiest of all the three questions. 2. Debugging Section (20 mins): ●There was an option to choose your Java, C++ and Python. ●This Section involved 7 easy debugging questions. ●I was able to 6 questions completely. 3. Aptitude Section (20 mins): ●General Mathematical Questions were asked (Around the 11th, and 12th levels) mainly consisting of topics like Permutation & Combination, Profit & Loss, Seating Arrangements and Statistics. Most of them are easy but due to time constraints, most students are not able to solve all of them. ●There were 10 questions out of which I solved 6 of them entirely and then I guessed the rest 4 of them as there was no negative marking (🙂). This concluded the Online Assessment and the result was declared on 31st July ( One day before the interview 🙂 ). 15 students were shortlisted for interviews. Interview: The interview with Morgan Stanley was conducted offline at the TPO office. We were supposed to be at the TPO office on or before 8 AM. Round 1: In this round, the interviewer usually asks you questions related to DBMS, OOPS, OS and DSA. In my case, I was asked mostly questions on subjective topics. They asked me only one DSA question but it highly depends on the interviewers. Some of the questions that I can recall are : ●Tell us something about yourself. ( This is a very important question and you should answer it as smoothly as possible and also mentions things in which you are good at first so if you are good at DSA/CP mention it first and then mention things related to your projects and other things. Also, don’t take more than 1-2 mins to answer this question.) ●In one sentence, How would you describe OOPS? ●Using an example of a motorcycle explain the 4 pillars of OOPS ●Some questions related to polymorphism like virtual functions, pure virtual functions, run time polymorphism vs compile time polymorphism. ●Some conceptual questions related to Inheritance and its use. ●What is DBMS? ●Some questions are related to different types of keys in DBMS. ●What is normalization, Explain different forms of normalization and ideally up to which normal form we should apply to normalize. ●Why do you use C++ and C vs C++? ●A standard question on some OS concepts like semaphores and deadlock. ●Then they asked me some questions related to my projects. ●Almost all the questions they asked me were testing my understanding of the topic just knowing the definition won’t work. They asked me only one DSA question : Given an array of non-negative numbers print all the sets of sizes greater than 1 having the sum of numbers equal to k. Initially, I gave them a recursive brute force approach and then we had a small discussion related to stack and heap memory. Then they asked me to optimize the solution. I was thinking of some way to optimize but they said no need to optimize (might be due to less time) just write code for the brute force which I wrote on a paper. There were some bugs which I resolved while doing a dry run over the sample test case given by them. The last 10 mins were sort of a rapid-fire round, They asked me questions which had answers only in one line. At the end of every round interviewer always asks you whether or not you have a question for them. You should always ask some questions, it shows that you are interested in the company. Overall the interview was of 1hr and 15 mins long. Out of 15, 11 students got the opportunity to interview for the next round. HR Round: This round is to judge your personality, your strengths, your weaknesses, your capability to handle the role, to check your background, and to understand if you're the right fit for this job. ●He asked me to introduce myself. ●Then he asked me questions like how I got admitted to VJTI, How I prepared for it, What were the challenges I faced during the preparation, How I handled them, etc. ●Then He asked me about my projects and He mainly focused on my group project. ●He asked about the tech stack I used and the reasons behind using the stack. ●He asked some situational questions like ○What would you do if someone from my group is not working as promised by him/her? ○If you were given a random real-world problem like poverty, How would you try to solve it? ○You are asked by your company to select places to set up petrol pump, What parameter would you take into consideration ●Then he asked me the following question: ○You have a computer with 10 GB RAM and a file of 9.5GB containing strings on each line. Sort the strings based on their lexicographical order. I didn’t understand the problem initially but then I realized that if we import a file of 9.5GB into RAM we will only have 0.5GB of memory for our program to run So if we use an algorithm which uses recursion (merge sort, quick sort) we will not sufficient memory. So I said we can use a more time-consuming algorithm like insertion sort which takes O(1) memory. He didn’t say whether or not my solution is correct. That was the last question he asked me and said If I had any questions for him. I asked a question and he answered it and this ended round 2 or HR round. Results were announced after a week ( actually they were waiting for DE Shaw to complete its process first as it was the first company). Out of 11, 8 were selected and I was fortunate to be one of them. Tips: For Online Assessment: ●Practice questions from Geeksforgeeks and Leetcode. You can also follow any sheet. for example - 450DSA by Love Babbar. ●Although It is not necessary but having some experience in Competitive programming will give you an extra edge and you will be afraid of any new questions you might get (It helped me to solve 2nd problem of OA as I knew how we make a tree similar to a graph while rest of them were trying to make node based tree which is a very time-consuming way to make a tree ). ●If the test contains Aptitude questions, they generally include Probability, PnC, Logic-based, Statistics, Math based puzzles, etc. Practice some questions from the Geeksforgeeks. For Interview: ●Write down your introduction and try to remember it by heart. ●Be confident while answering the questions and remember if you pronounced some words incorrectly or fumbled in between they will not reject you for that. ●Be honest. if you don’t know a topic just let them know and don’t mention projects, in your resume, that you haven’t worked on. ●Also, in your resume, if you have mentioned any group project always mention what did you do in particular. ●Don’t cheat during OA. ●Whenever the interviewer asks you a question, make sure that you understand the question correctly and I would suggest you that repeat whatever you understand again so that the interviewer can repeat the question again if you misunderstand something. ●While preparing for subjective topics like DBMS, etc. try to understand things with real-world examples rather than mugging the definitions and try to remember an example for each topic you learn. ●Go through some standard HR questions one day before the interview so that you can be prepared for those questions. ●Stay hydrated during the interview. ●Believe in yourself. ●Don’t get demotivated by rejections, try to analyze what went wrong and work on that part. Resources: ●For DSA - GeeksforGeeks, Leetcode, YT channel of Aditya Verma. ●For CP - Codeforces, Codechef. ●For OS - Gate Smashers playlist, InterviewBit-Questions. ●For DBMS - Gate Smashers Playlist, InterviewBit-Questions. ●For OOPS - GeeksforGeeks.
